chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: Yank Lawson, Bob Haggart and Ed Hall
summary: He found Yank Lawson drinks but is good-natured, Bob Haggart is sober, and Ed Hall had just died when he joined.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah. What's the trumpet player's name?
Yeah. Did you get along with him?
Yeah, I got along with -- all right with all of them.
Isn't he a little hard to get along with?
His big problem is drinking, too, see.
And when he gets drunk, he doesn't care about anybody.
Anybody, as far as that's concerned.
He's a different type of guy from Bob Haggert, really.
And that's the reason why he went on the wagon. He's an A.A., Bob Haggert.
And so he and his wife both went on that together, see. So he doesn't drink anything.
Offer him a drink. He doesn't know how to say no. But he's a nice guy. He's like Mr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. He gets drunk and that's -- his big problem is his drinking. But he's a great guy.
Oh, I'm so glad to hear you say that.
And, of course, -- so Ed Hall was with the band.
Yeah, well, he wasn't with the band when I got in there.
Oh, he died then. Oh, yeah.
